Trace plots and other MCMC plots with bayesplot

Source: R/plot-mcmc.R
plot_mcmc.Rd

plot_mcmc() is a convenience wrapper around bayesplot functions for the posterior draws of a fit: trace plots, rank plots and densities by chain, pairs plots, and the energy plot of the sampler. For any other plot, pass the draws (x$draws) and bayesplot::nuts_params(x) to bayesplot directly.

Usage

plot_mcmc(
  x,
  type = c("trace", "rank", "dens", "pairs", "energy"),
  pars = c("alpha", "lambda", "mean_g", "sd_g"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

type

Type of plot: "trace" (the default), "rank", "dens", "pairs" or "energy". See Details.

pars

Character vector with the names of the parameters to plot. A name without an index selects all elements of that parameter, e.g., "alpha" selects every spline coefficient. By default the spline coefficients, lambda, and the mean and standard deviation of \(g\) are plotted. Not used with type = "energy".

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

The object returned by the bayesplot function: a ggplot object or, for type = "pairs", a grid of plots that is shown when it is printed.

Details

Each type calls one bayesplot function: "trace" calls mcmc_trace(), "rank" calls mcmc_rank_overlay(), "dens" calls mcmc_dens_overlay(), "pairs" calls mcmc_pairs() (which also marks the divergent transitions), and "energy" calls mcmc_nuts_energy(). The bayesplot package must be installed, and the plots use its theme and colors. type = "pairs" also needs the gridExtra package.

Only the draws stored in the fit are plotted. If the fit was thinned (thin), these are a subset of the iterations, whereas diagnose() and plot_diagnostics() describe the whole run. The energy plot compares the energy at each iteration with its change from the previous iteration, so it needs every iteration. For a thinned fit, including the fits stored in the package, type = "energy" therefore throws an error. In that case diagnose() still reports the E-BFMI of the whole run.

In a trace plot, chains that have converged cover the same range and none of them drifts. See vignette("diagnostics") and vignette("plots") for how to read the trace plot and the rank plot.

See also

plot_diagnostics(), diagnose(), vignette("diagnostics")

Examples

plot_mcmc(krw_fit, pars = c("lambda", "mean_g", "sd_g"))

plot_mcmc(krw_fit, type = "rank", pars = "alpha")

plot_mcmc(krw_fit, type = "dens", pars = c("mean_g", "sd_g"))
